items.title: GIFT Nifty signals muted start for Dalal Street amid cautious trade
items.description: Indian markets experienced a volatile session ahead of monthly expiry, with the Nifty closing lower at 23,866. Geopolitical tensions in West Asia are expected to keep investor sentiment cautious, despite a dip in crude oil prices. Analysts suggest a mixed trend for equities, with the Nifty potentially hovering around 24,000, but a break below 23,800 could signal a correction.

items.title: Stocks in news: Kotak Mahindra Bank, Tata Motors, HDFC Bank, IndiGo, Coal India
items.description: Indian markets experienced a volatile yet narrow trading range, concluding marginally lower as consolidation persists. Analysts await a decisive breakout above 24,200. Key stocks like Tata Motors, HDFC Bank, IndiGo, Coal India, and Kotak Mahindra Bank are in focus due to significant developments including new product launches, executive appointments, and strategic investments. Coal India plans substantial R&D spending to enhance productivity and reduce emissions.

items.title: Extended Nifty consolidation may be setting up the next bull run: Edelweiss MF study
items.description: Indian stock markets have seen a flat performance recently, but historical data suggests this could be a precursor to stronger gains.  A study indicates that after similar periods of stagnation, the Nifty has historically delivered robust returns over one and three-year horizons.  Fund managers believe large-cap stocks, now trading at attractive valuations, offer a favorable risk-reward profile for patient investors.

items.title: Sebi moves to standardise consent rules for AIFs
items.description: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is proposing significant governance changes for alternative investment funds. The regulator aims to standardize investor consent, enhance oversight of conflict-of-interest deals, and introduce a uniform 75% approval threshold for key decisions. This move seeks to address inconsistencies in current rules and ensure greater transparency and fairness for investors across all AIF regulations.

items.title: Dalal Street bets on a strong July as macro risks begin to fade
items.description: Indian equities are poised for a positive July, building on historical trends and recent market strengths. Easing crude oil prices, a stable rupee, and reduced foreign selling are fueling optimism. Analysts anticipate the Nifty could climb 2-3% from current levels, with mid and small-cap stocks expected to lead the rally. Investors are closely watching geopolitical developments and monsoon progress for further market catalysts.

items.title: These 7 private and public banking stocks have an upside of up to 24% in one year, according to analysts
items.description: At the end of the day, both private and PSU banks are equally impacted by what goes on in the economy. If they are behaving differently in the market these days, it is because of valuations, existing ownership, overall fund flows, and the kind of investors putting in the money. Check out Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, for price targets of over 4,000 listed stocks along with detailed company analysis focusing on five key components, earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum, to generate standardised scores. SR+ Reports is a complimentary offering to ETPrime members.

items.title: Kotak to buy Deutsche's India retail, wealth business
items.description: Kotak Mahindra Bank is set to acquire Deutsche Bank's retail, private banking, and wealth management operations in India. This significant deal, involving approximately ₹29,000 crore in loans and ₹16,000 crore in deposits, will bring around 150,000 new customers and 1,000 employees to Kotak. The acquisition aims to bolster Kotak's focus on affluent and SME clients, while Deutsche Bank streamlines its global portfolio.

items.title: JSW taps KKR to drive in MG Motors JV with $400 mn investment
items.description: A combination of primary infusion and secondary share sale is planned as valuation doubles to $3 billion in 3 years. Sajjan Jindal led group is set to emerge as the single largest shareholder in the country's 3rd largest EV passenger car maker.

items.title: AM/NS takes over banks' claims linked to Essar Group promoters' personal guarantees
items.description: "Banks had claims attached to the personal guarantees issued by the Essar promoters which was linked to the Essar Steel resolution. AM/NS' plan had made specific provisions to pay off these liabilities too, but there were some legal issues which are now resolved, allowing banks and AM/NS to complete this deal," said a person familiar with the details.

items.title: Don't worry, banks have shock absorbers: RBI
items.description: In its bi-annual Financial Stability Report, the RBI flagged concerns over customer service in the insurance sector and again cautioned that rising interconnectedness among financial institutions could act as a potential channel for contagion. The report noted that cybersecurity risks have emerged as a key financial stability concern.

items.title: Solvency buffers at insurers thinning; general insurance sector more of a concern
items.description: The Reserve Bank of India's latest report highlights concerns over thinning capital in the insurance sector. While life insurers remain compliant, their buffers are shrinking. The general insurance segment faces a more serious challenge, with three public sector firms persistently falling below the minimum solvency requirement for over a year, posing a direct financial stability risk.

items.title: Banks clear RBI stress test, but NPAs tick up in tough scenarios
items.description: The Reserve Bank of India's latest financial stability report indicates that Indian banks will likely keep capital levels above the regulatory minimum, even in challenging scenarios. Core capital ratios may see some reduction, but they are anticipated to remain healthy. On the other hand, certain NBFCs could experience difficulties.

items.title: Household sector debt climbs to 45.5% of GDP in Sep 2025: RBI report
items.description: Household debt has climbed to 45.5% of India's GDP, driven by a surge in non-housing retail loans, now making up over half of total borrowings. Despite this rise, borrower quality is improving, with more prime borrowers taking out loans. While consumption loans dominate, experts express concern over debt servicing for depreciating assets. India ranks fourth among emerging economies in household debt as a percentage of GDP.

items.title: Advit Jewels share price tanks 5% after strong 37% market debut. Should you buy, sell or hold?
items.description: Advit Jewels shares made a strong stock market debut, listing at a 37% premium to the IPO price before trimming gains. While analysts remain positive on the company's growth prospects and improving financials, they advise fresh investors to wait for more earnings visibility amid risks linked to commodity prices and business concentration.

items.title: KPIT Tech shares hit by downgrades, target price cuts. What JPMorgan and other brokerages said
items.description: KPIT Technologies shares plunged after the company issued a weak preliminary Q1 FY27 business update, prompting several brokerages, including JPMorgan and JM Financial, to downgrade the stock and cut target prices. While analysts remain optimistic about the company's long-term prospects, they expect near-term earnings and growth to remain under pressure.

items.title: India's $2 billion state stake sales buck equity market slowdown
items.description: India's government secured a significant $2 billion from stake sales in state-run companies last quarter, a rare positive for the subdued capital market.  This substantial divestment, primarily from Coal India and NHPC, provided a crucial boost to non-tax revenue amidst global market volatility and geopolitical concerns. The move highlights the government's strategy to bolster finances through public sector asset sales.

items.title: Only 1/5th the size of NSE? Why Jefferies predicts 27% upside for this near-monopoly stock
items.description: Jefferies has initiated coverage on MCX with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 3,600, implying 27% upside. The brokerage expects strong earnings growth, driven by rising retail participation in commodity derivatives, new product launches, and multiple growth catalysts, while highlighting the exchange’s near-monopoly position in non-agri contracts.

items.title: CarTrade Tech shares rocket 6% as Nomura raises target price. Here are 3 reasons why
items.description: CarTrade Tech shares rose after Nomura reiterated its 'Buy' rating and raised its target price, citing stronger growth prospects for OLX. The brokerage expects artificial intelligence-led monetisation, new revenue streams, expanding margins and rising adoption of financing, escrow and logistics services to support long-term earnings growth.

items.title: Zee Entertainment shares jump 6% after Rs 418 crore FDI approval
items.description: Zee Entertainment shares jumped after receiving government approval for a Rs 418 crore foreign investment from an Invesco-managed fund. This marks the fund's return to ZEEL's shareholder base after a previous exit. The investment comes as the company navigates challenges in its broadcasting business but sees improvements in its digital segment.  FDI inflows into India's information and broadcasting sector also saw a significant rise.

items.title: Ola Electric doubles QoQ growth in Q1 FY26; June vehicle registrations at 16,144 units
items.description: Ola Electric witnessed a significant surge in electric two-wheeler registrations during the April-June quarter, nearly doubling from the previous period. This impressive growth, reaching 43,719 vehicles, is attributed to enhanced retail operations, better product availability, and consistent customer demand. The company registered its highest monthly sales in June, signaling a strong recovery in market momentum and underscoring its commitment to expanding EV adoption in India.

items.title: Why KPIT Tech shares crashed 15% today: The BMW & Volkswagen connection explained
items.description: KPIT Technologies shares fell after the company warned of an unexpected slowdown in revenue from European auto clients, likely including BMW and Volkswagen. In a Q1FY27 update, the firm said it now expects a ~1% YoY revenue decline, citing sudden cutbacks by European OEMs following weak earnings outlooks.

items.title: Reliance Power shares soar 18%, snap 4-day losing streak. What’s triggering the sharp surge?
items.description: Reliance Power shares rose sharply on Wednesday, snapping a four-day losing streak after the company announced plans to expand into artificial intelligence and technology-driven businesses through its subsidiaries. The company renamed four subsidiaries to reflect the AI-focused strategy, boosting investor sentiment despite weak recent financial performance.

items.title: From niche to mainstream: How India's bond market reinvented itself over the last 10 years
items.description: India's bond market has transformed significantly over the last decade, moving from an opaque, institutional-focused space to a more transparent and accessible one. Regulatory reforms, technological advancements, and global index inclusion have fueled this growth, nearly tripling total issuances. Experts highlight reduced minimum investment thresholds and enhanced regulatory frameworks as key drivers, paving the way for substantial future expansion.

items.title: Vedanta Iron & Steel shares skyrocket 89% in 12 days since listing. What’s fuelling the surge?
items.description: Vedanta Iron and Steel shares have surged an impressive 89% since their June debut, adding nearly Rs 7,000 crore to its market value. This remarkable rally was significantly boosted after Azim Premji's investment arm acquired shares worth Rs 102 crore. The company, involved in iron ore and steel production across India and Africa, is currently clarifying significant price movements with stock exchanges.

items.title: Silent winners! 43 stocks turned multibaggers even as Nifty went nowhere in 2 years
items.description: Despite the Nifty 50 showing minimal returns over two years, astute investors have witnessed significant wealth creation. Forty-three stocks have more than doubled investor wealth, with companies in defence, healthcare, and specialty chemicals leading the charge. This period highlights that market opportunities often lie beneath the surface of headline index movements, rewarding patient stock pickers.

items.title: Sensex rises over 150 points, Nifty above 23,900 as investors weigh Iran tensions, weak monsoon concerns
items.description: Indian stock markets opened the second half of 2026 with modest gains after recent declines. Investors are closely watching escalating US-Iran tensions, which are impacting oil prices, and a concerningly weak monsoon season. Analysts suggest adjusting portfolios towards fixed income and monsoon-proof sectors like healthcare and defense to mitigate potential fallout from the dry spell.

items.title: Railtel Corp shares gain over 2% after firm wins Rs 108 crore order from Mahanadi Coalfields
items.description: Railtel Corporation's shares surged after announcing a significant Rs 107.61 crore order from Mahanadi Coalfields for an MPLS VPN network. This follows another recent win from Thane Municipal Corporation for a citizen engagement platform and a Goa Labour Welfare Board portal. Despite recent short-term dips, the company shows strong long-term returns and robust quarterly earnings growth, with revenue up 28% year-on-year.

items.title: Cupid shares gain 2% as firm raises FY27 guidance, expects Q1 revenue to top Rs 150 crore
items.description: Cupid shares gained 2% as the company anticipates a record Q1 FY27 revenue exceeding Rs 150 crore.  Buoyed by strong market visibility, Cupid has boosted its FY27 revenue forecast to over Rs 660 crore. This optimistic outlook is fueled by diversified business, expanding global opportunities in healthcare, and growth in its condom and lubricant portfolios.  The company is also making strides in its IVD business, signaling robust future potential.

items.title: Rs 19 lakh crore shocker! TCS, Infosys & 2 IT giants crash 50% from peak: Is the absolute worst yet to come?
items.description: India's top IT firms, including TCS and Infosys, have seen their market value plummet by at least 50% from peak levels, erasing nearly Rs 19.28 lakh crore. This brutal correction is fueled by macroeconomic stress in North America and the disruptive potential of generative AI. Analysts warn of further de-rating as the sector grapples with these structural changes and cautious global economic outlooks.
